title: Canada Announces Retaliatory Tariffs on $20B of US Goods, Effective September 8
detail: Three days after US-Canada trade talks collapsed and Washington's 50% Section 338 tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian autos, alcohol, and dairy took effect (Aug 22), Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada's countermeasures: tiered retaliatory tariffs of 15%, 25%, and 50% on roughly $20 billion of US goods across 700+ products, effective September 8. The 50% tier hits steel, aluminum, furniture, and clothing; 25% covers appliances, dairy, and seafood; 15% applies to other industrial goods, plus everyday items like electronics, pulp/paper, and cosmetics. Carney said Canada would match Washington's tariffs 'dollar for dollar to protect Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses,' and separately unveiled a C$7.5 billion (US$5.4 billion) support package for affected workers and businesses.

title: US Stocks Rally as Chip Sector Rebounds and Investors Brush Aside Canada Trade Tensions Ahead of Nvidia Earnings
detail: US equities gained Tuesday as investors looked past the Canada tariff escalation and rotated back into semiconductor names ahead of Nvidia's Wednesday earnings report. The S&P 500 rose 24.42 points (+0.3%) to 7,677.28, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 160.24 points (+0.3%) to 53,577.40, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 171.11 points (+0.7%) to 26,151.30. Nvidia shares gained about 2%, snapping a seven-day losing streak. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 7 basis points to 4.625%, easing off the prior week's 19-year highs, while markets also weighed expectations for incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech (Aug 28).
